To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ASCs may favour cancer recurrence via HGP/c-Met signaling and that c-Met positivity in primary breast cancer could be predictive of risk for cancer recurrence after autolous fat graft in breast cancer patients.
ASCs are able to enhance tumorigenic behaviour and recurrence of c-Met-positive breast cancer cells, by creating an inflammatory microenvirontment which sustained tumor growth.
ASCs, in the absence of a c-Met activation, are not able to promote a tumorigenic transformation in normal breast cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the interactions between adipose-derived mesenchimal stem cells and breast cancer cells.
the potential tumorigenicity of ASCs in breast cancer recurrence and the possible involvement of the HGF/c-MET pathway in this phenomenon.
the safety of ASCs in fat grafts, which could be used as an adjuvant therapy in breast cancer, in order to prevent tumor recurrence and metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ASCs, per se, are not tumorigenesis but, in the context of breast cancer, can exacerbate the tumor growth, angiogenesis, metastasis and cancer stemness, via HGF/cMet signaling.
ASCs are safe for breast cancer patients, however, in the presence of a strong c-Met expression in the primary tumor, the use of fat grafts could be contraindicated.
ASCs, per se, are not tumorigenically active but they can support tumor cells growth and metastasis, by sustaining the c-Met/HGF axis, thus increasing the risk of recurrence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autologous adipose tissue grafts are not tumourigenic per se, but may favour cancer recurrence via HFG/c-Met signalling.
ASCs are safe in clinical application, but they could exacerbate the tumor growth in c-Met expressing patients.
autologous ASC transplantation in breast cancer patients is safe, as ASCs are not able to exert an oncogenic role per sè.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ASCs are able to enhance tumour growth and recurrence via c-Met/HGF pathway, suggesting the need for a careful selection of breast cancer patients for fat grafting.

c-Met is a potential marker of recurrence after fat graft in post-mastectomy cancer patients, and that c-Met inhibitors may represent a new strategy to prevent breast cancer recurrence in patients who underwent a fat graft procedure for breast reconstruction.
ASCs are safe in fat graft for post-surgical breast cancer patients, provided that c-Met is not expressed in the tumor.
